deliverables.title: Local inference on LIBR compute, and the fleet it is becoming

threads.title: The everyday server (ollama, user-local)
threads.question: Serves the coding models on one A40 from a user-local install. No admin rights anywhere in it. Serving is done; what is left on it is the walltime note in the plan's housekeeping section.

threads.title: Up, code, down (bin/ollama-*)
threads.question: Three scripts that submit the job, wait until it is really serving, and open an agent on its node.

threads.title: The coding agent (opencode, and its fence)
threads.question: opencode on the serving node, with web access denied globally and raised for one agent only.

threads.title: The consultant (colibri, GLM-5.2 int4)
threads.question: 744B on most of a 1 TB node, one user at a time, for work that cannot leave the building. Serving is done. Two questions are open: how many KV slots, and whether MTP should be forced off.

threads.title: The five colibri commands (bin/coli*)
threads.question: Build, submit, ask, code and cancel. Each finds the job through squeue and steps onto its node. coli-ask is the interactive one and coli-code is the overnight one: the preamble is the bill.

threads.title: The engine (vendor/colibri-build/c)
threads.question: The int4 GLM kernel, built at a pinned commit. ARCH=native is what selects the fast path. It lives outside this repository, in the Atlas checkout, and is not in git. Rebuild after a clone.

threads.title: Keeping upstream current (a daily user timer)
threads.question: Pulls the read-only colibri clone once a day. Never build in it; the timer expects a clean tree.

threads.title: The measurement campaign (P0)
threads.question: Twelve tests that decide the fleet's shape. Ten have passed and fifteen findings contradict the runbook.

threads.title: The fleet
threads.question: Three engines behind one front door, taking GPUs when free and yielding them when somebody else is blocked. Designed in full in DESIGN.md and scheduled in FLEET-BUILD.md. None of it is built.
